Canada Threatens Cleveland-Cliffs With Forced Sale of Assets Over Layoff Plans

OTTAWA--Canada's federal government formally demanded on Thursday that steel maker Cleveland-Cliffs abandon plans to lay off Canadian workers, adding that failure to comply could lead to a fine or a forced sale of the company's Canadian assets.

Canadian Industry Minister Melanie Joly said the company's layoff plans, affecting workers at two Ontario plants, would violate commitments the U.S. company made when it secured Canadian approval for its 2024 takeover of Stelco.

"No act of God or change in market conditions can relieve Cleveland-Cliffs of the commitments it made to Canada. Those commitments are not optional," Joly said in a statement posted on the social-media platform X.

Cliffs Chief Executive Lourenco Goncalves told The Wall Street Journal last week the company hasn't breached the law and that a temporary reduction in headcount is needed as it refocuses its operations to counter the pressure on the industry from U.S. tariffs.
